title: 2 Samuel Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 6.

questions.question: How many chosen men of Israel did David gather together?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:1 states that David gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

questions.question: From where did David and all the people arise to bring up the ark of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Baale of Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:2 specifies that David arose and went with all the people from Baale of Judah to bring up the ark of God.

questions.question: What was the ark of God set upon when taken out of the house of Abinadab?
questions.correctAnswer: A new cart
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:3 says they set the ark of God upon a new cart to bring it out of the house of Abinadab.

questions.question: Who were the sons of Abinadab that drove the new cart?
questions.correctAnswer: Uzzah and Ahio
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:3 identifies Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, as those who drove the new cart.

questions.question: Who went before the ark when it was brought out of the house of Abinadab?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahio
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:4 states that Ahio went before the ark as they brought it out.

questions.question: What types of instruments did David and all the house of Israel play before the LORD?
options: Harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets, and cymbals
questions.correctAnswer: Harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets, and cymbals
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:5 lists these instruments as those played before the LORD by David and all Israel.

questions.question: At which location did Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Nachon's threshingfloor
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:6 says that when they came to Nachon's threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark.

questions.question: Why did Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God?
options: To steady it because the oxen shook it
questions.correctAnswer: To steady it because the oxen shook it
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:6 explains that Uzzah took hold of the ark because the oxen shook it.

questions.question: What was the consequence of Uzzah's action of touching the ark?
options: He was smitten by God and died
questions.correctAnswer: He was smitten by God and died
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:7 records that the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah, and God smote him there for his error; and he died by the ark of God.

questions.question: What name did David give to the place where Uzzah died?
questions.correctAnswer: Perezuzzah
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:8 states that David called the name of the place Perezuzzah because of the breach made upon Uzzah.

questions.question: True or False: David was pleased and joyful when Uzzah was smitten for touching the ark.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:8 says David was displeased because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzzah.

questions.question: True or False: The ark of God was brought from the house of Abinadab in Gibeah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:3 confirms the ark was brought out of the house of Abinadab in Gibeah.

questions.question: True or False: Uzzah was smitten because he disobeyed God's command by touching the ark.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:7 explains that God smote Uzzah for his error when he touched the ark, showing it was against God's command.

questions.question: True or False: Ahio went behind the ark as it was brought out of the house of Abinadab.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:4 states that Ahio went before the ark, not behind it.

questions.question: Which action took place first in 2 Samuel 6?
options: The ark was placed on a new cart
questions.correctAnswer: David gathered thirty thousand men
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:1 shows David first gathered thirty thousand men before any other listed event.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Why was David afraid on the day the ark of the LORD was brought toward him?
options: Because he feared the LORD due to Uzzah's death
Because he doubted the people's loyalty
Because the oxen were too weak to carry the ark
Because the ark was lost temporarily
questions.correctAnswer: Because he feared the LORD due to Uzzah's death
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:7 describes how God smote Uzzah for touching the ark, and 2 Samuel 6:9 explains David's fear of the LORD that day, showing a direct connection between Uzzah's death and David's fear.

questions.question: What did David do with the ark of the LORD after he was afraid?
options: He took it to the house of Obededom the Gittite
He placed it directly in the city of David
He returned it to the house of Abinadab
He left it at Nachon's threshingfloor
questions.correctAnswer: He took it to the house of Obededom the Gittite
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:10 states that David would not bring the ark into the city of David immediately but carried it aside into Obededom's house, showing his caution after the incident.

questions.question: How long did the ark remain in the house of Obededom the Gittite?
questions.correctAnswer: Three months
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:11 clearly states the ark stayed in Obededom's house for three months, during which the LORD blessed Obededom and his household.

questions.question: What was the significance of the blessing on Obededom's household while the ark was with them?
options: It showed that the ark brought God's favor wherever it dwelt
It was a sign to return the ark to Abinadab's house
It indicated the need to build a temple immediately
It meant the ark should be moved away to avoid danger
questions.correctAnswer: It showed that the ark brought God's favor wherever it dwelt
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:11-12 explain the LORD blessed Obededom's household because of the ark, teaching that God's presence brings blessing and favor.

questions.question: What motivated David to finally bring the ark into the city of David with gladness?
options: The report that the LORD blessed Obededom's house
questions.correctAnswer: The report that the LORD blessed Obededom's house
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:12 shows that when David heard about the LORD's blessing on Obededom, he was encouraged and brought the ark into the city with gladness.

questions.question: What did the person carrying the ark do after going six paces?
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrificed oxen and fatlings
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:13 states that after six paces, the bearer of the ark sacrificed oxen and fatlings, showing reverence and thanksgiving to God during the procession.

questions.question: How did David express his worship before the LORD when bringing the ark into the city?
options: He danced with all his might, girded with a linen ephod
He sat silently as a sign of humility
He sang psalms but did not dance
questions.correctAnswer: He danced with all his might, girded with a linen ephod
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:14 describes David dancing with all his might before the LORD while wearing a linen ephod, illustrating wholehearted and joyful worship.

questions.question: What accompanied the procession of the ark into the city according to 2 Samuel 6:15?
options: Shouting and the sound of the trumpet
questions.correctAnswer: Shouting and the sound of the trumpet
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:15 states that David and all Israel brought up the ark with shouting and the sound of the trumpet, emphasizing exuberant worship.

questions.question: How did Michal, Saul's daughter, react when she saw David dancing before the LORD?
options: She despised him in her heart
questions.correctAnswer: She despised him in her heart
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:16 reveals Michal saw David leaping and dancing and despised him in her heart, showing a contrast in responses to David's worship.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 6:17 teach about David's actions after bringing in the ark?
options: He set the ark in a tabernacle and offered burnt and peace offerings
He immediately built a temple for the ark
He hid the ark in a secret place
He returned the ark to Obededom
questions.correctAnswer: He set the ark in a tabernacle and offered burnt and peace offerings
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:17 states that the ark was placed in the tabernacle David pitched for it, and he offered burnt and peace offerings, showing devotion and obedience.

questions.question: How does the passage show the importance of generosity after worship?
options: David gave bread, flesh, and wine to all the people after blessing them
David kept all the offerings for himself
The people were told to fast after the ceremony
questions.correctAnswer: David gave bread, flesh, and wine to all the people after blessing them
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:19 describes David distributing food and wine to everyone, men and women alike, teaching generosity and sharing blessings with others.

questions.question: How does David's response to Michal's criticism illustrate humility and devotion?
options: He said he danced before the LORD who chose him to rule
He ignored her and stopped worshiping
He left the city in shame
questions.correctAnswer: He said he danced before the LORD who chose him to rule
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:21 shows David explaining his worship as an act before the LORD who appointed him, indicating his humility and devotion despite criticism.

questions.question: What lesson about personal humility can be drawn from David's statement in 2 Samuel 6:22?
options: He is willing to be even more lowly in his own sight to honor God
He seeks to elevate himself above others
He wants to be honored by the maidservants only
questions.correctAnswer: He is willing to be even more lowly in his own sight to honor God
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:22 describes David's willingness to be 'more vile' and 'base' in his own eyes, teaching that true worship involves humility and lowliness before God.

questions.question: What was the lasting consequence for Michal after her contempt toward David's worship?
options: She had no children until the day of her death
She was forgiven and blessed with many children
questions.correctAnswer: She had no children until the day of her death
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:23 states that Michal had no children until her death, suggesting a consequence linked to her attitude toward David's worship.

questions.question: True or False: David immediately brought the ark into the city of David without hesitation after Uzzah's death.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:9-10 show David was afraid and did not immediately bring the ark into the city but placed it in Obededom's house first, indicating hesitation.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 6.

questions.question: Where was the ark of the LORD set when it was brought into the city of David?
options: In the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it
On a new cart in Gibeah
questions.correctAnswer: In the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:17 states that the ark was set in its place in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it, indicating a specially prepared place for the ark.

questions.question: What offerings did David make before the LORD after setting the ark in its place?
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt offerings and peace offerings
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 6:17, David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD after placing the ark.

questions.question: After completing the offerings, what did David do to the people?
options: Blessed them in the name of the LORD of hosts
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed them in the name of the LORD of hosts
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:18 states that after the offerings, David blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts, showing his leadership role and God's favor.

questions.question: What items did David distribute among the entire multitude of Israel?
options: A cake of bread, a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine
questions.correctAnswer: A cake of bread, a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:19 explains that David dealt among all the people a cake of bread, a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine, showing generosity and celebration.

questions.question: How did Michal, Saul's daughter, react when she saw David dancing before the LORD?
options: She despised him in her heart
questions.correctAnswer: She despised him in her heart
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:16 states Michal looked through a window, saw David dancing, and despised him in her heart, showing her disapproval of David's behavior.

questions.question: What did Michal say to David regarding his behavior before the handmaids?
options: How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself shamelessly
You have acted wisely before the LORD
Your dancing pleased the people of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself shamelessly
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:20 records Michal rebuking David for uncovering himself before the handmaids, calling him shameless.

questions.question: How did David justify his behavior in front of Michal?
options: He said it was before the LORD who chose him to be ruler over Israel
He said he wanted to impress the people
He apologized and promised to stop
questions.correctAnswer: He said it was before the LORD who chose him to be ruler over Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:21 records David explaining that his dancing was before the LORD who chose him over Saul and his house to be ruler over Israel.

questions.question: What did David say he would do in the future regarding his behavior before the LORD?
options: He would be even more vile and base in his own sight
He would be more careful and modest
He would only dance in private
questions.correctAnswer: He would be even more vile and base in his own sight
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:22 shows David declaring he would be more vile and base in his own sight, showing his humility and devotion despite Michal’s criticism.

questions.question: What was the consequence for Michal, Saul's daughter, mentioned at the end of the chapter?
options: She had no child until the day of her death
questions.correctAnswer: She had no child until the day of her death
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:23 states Michal had no child to the day of her death, possibly connected to her contempt for David’s worship.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to David’s dancing before the LORD?
options: Exodus 15:20-21, where Miriam leads women in dance after crossing the Red Sea
Leviticus 16, the Day of Atonement rituals
Numbers 13, the spying out of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 15:20-21, where Miriam leads women in dance after crossing the Red Sea
questions.explanation: David’s joyful dance before the LORD (2 Samuel 6:14) echoes earlier biblical themes of worship through dance, such as Miriam’s dance in Exodus 15:20-21 celebrating deliverance.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of rejoicing and worship before God as seen in David’s actions?
options: Luke 15:25, the parable of the prodigal son’s celebration
Acts 2:1-4, the coming of the Holy Spirit
Romans 8:28, God working all things for good
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 15:25, the parable of the prodigal son’s celebration
questions.explanation: David’s exuberant worship (2 Samuel 6:14) is echoed in Luke 15:25 where the father celebrates the return of the lost son with joy and dance, highlighting joyful worship before God.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew term 'ephod' mentioned in 2 Samuel 6:14 that David wore?
options: A linen priestly garment symbolizing service to God
A common garment worn by all Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: A linen priestly garment symbolizing service to God
questions.explanation: The 'ephod' (2 Samuel 6:14) was a sacred linen garment worn by priests, signifying David’s role in worship and service before the LORD.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the structure of 2 Samuel 6, especially regarding the ark’s journey and David’s reaction?
options: Inclusio framing the ark’s movement and worship
Chiasm focusing on the death of Uzzah
Parallelism between David and Michal’s reactions
Alliteration in the naming of places
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the ark’s movement and worship
questions.explanation: The chapter uses inclusio by beginning and ending with the ark’s movement and David’s worship (2 Samuel 6:1-5 and 6:17-23), framing the narrative and emphasizing the central theme.

questions.question: True or False: David’s blessing of the people after offering sacrifices was limited to the men of Israel only.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:19 states David dealt among the whole multitude of Israel, both women and men, showing the blessing was inclusive.

questions.question: True or False: David’s intense dancing before the LORD was motivated by his awareness that God had chosen him over Saul to be ruler of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David explicitly states in 2 Samuel 6:21 that his dancing was before the LORD who chose him over Saul, revealing the motivation behind his worship.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the death of Uzzah for touching the ark reveal about God's nature in 2 Samuel 6:6-7?
options: God is indifferent to human actions
God demands holiness and reverence toward His presence
God accepts all forms of worship equally
questions.correctAnswer: God demands holiness and reverence toward His presence
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 show that when Uzzah touched the ark to steady it, God's anger was kindled and He struck Uzzah dead, demonstrating God's holiness and the necessity of reverence when approaching His presence. This aligns with the doctrine of God's holiness (Isaiah 6:3).

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 6:11 illustrate God's blessing in response to the ark's presence?
options: The house of Obededom was cursed
The house of Obededom was blessed
The ark brought destruction to Obededom's house
The presence of the ark had no effect on Obededom's household
questions.correctAnswer: The house of Obededom was blessed
questions.explanation: Verse 11 states the ark remained in Obededom's house for three months and the LORD blessed Obededom and his household, demonstrating God's blessing upon those who reverently receive His presence (cf. Numbers 6:24-26).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated in David's fear after Uzzah's death in 2 Samuel 6:9?
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness
questions.explanation: David's fear in verse 9 reflects a recognition of God's holiness and the awe due to Him, as God's pure and perfect nature demands respect and reverence (cf. Hebrews 12:28-29).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is taught by David's decision in 2 Samuel 6:10 to place the ark in Obededom's house rather than bringing it directly into the city?
options: The ark is merely a decorative object
God's presence cannot be treated lightly and requires proper respect
The ark had no significance for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God's presence cannot be treated lightly and requires proper respect
questions.explanation: David's hesitation and decision to place the ark in Obededom's house illustrates the doctrine that God's presence is holy and must be approached with caution and reverence (2 Samuel 6:10).

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 6:13-14, what does David's dancing before the LORD symbolize in terms of worship and sanctification?
options: Joyful, wholehearted worship as an expression of sanctified life
questions.correctAnswer: Joyful, wholehearted worship as an expression of sanctified life
questions.explanation: David danced with all his might and was girded with a linen ephod (v14), symbolizing joyous, sincere worship and personal consecration to God, reflecting sanctification (cf. Psalm 149:3-5).

questions.question: How does the narrative in 2 Samuel 6:16-23 involving Michal critique external religiosity versus internal devotion?
options: Michal despises David's genuine worship, showing hypocrisy
Michal leads the worship with David
Michal is indifferent to David's actions
questions.correctAnswer: Michal despises David's genuine worship, showing hypocrisy
questions.explanation: In verses 16 and 20, Michal despises David for dancing before the LORD, highlighting the tension between external appearances and heartfelt devotion. David defends his sincere worship in verse 21, emphasizing internal devotion over social judgment.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's blessing and human responsibility is conveyed in 2 Samuel 6:11 and 2 Samuel 6:19?
options: God blesses independently of human response
God's blessing is linked to reverence and communal sharing
Blessings are unrelated to worship or generosity
questions.correctAnswer: God's blessing is linked to reverence and communal sharing
questions.explanation: Verse 11 shows God blessing Obededom’s household because of the ark’s presence, and verse 19 describes David distributing food and wine to the people, illustrating that God's blessing involves both reverence toward Him and responsible communal generosity.

questions.question: What does the ark’s journey and David’s actions in 2 Samuel 6 teach about the foreshadowing of Christ’s redemptive work?
options: The ark symbolizes God's presence and Christ as mediator
The ark is unrelated to Christ
The ark was a mere cultural artifact
questions.correctAnswer: The ark symbolizes God's presence and Christ as mediator
questions.explanation: The ark represents the presence of God among His people, foreshadowing Christ who is the ultimate presence of God and mediator (cf. John 1:14; Hebrews 9:4). David's reverence shows the recognition of God's holiness in Christ.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God's justice and mercy can be drawn from the contrasting events of Uzzah’s death (2 Samuel 6:7) and Obededom’s blessing (2 Samuel 6:11)?
options: God is unjust in punishing Uzzah
God’s justice demands holiness, but His mercy blesses the obedient
God only shows mercy, not justice
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice demands holiness, but His mercy blesses the obedient
questions.explanation: Uzzah’s death demonstrates God's justice and holiness requiring obedience, while Obededom’s blessing shows God's mercy toward those who reverently receive His presence, illustrating the balance of divine justice and mercy.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 6:17-18 reveal the proper response to God's presence in worship and leadership?
options: Offerings and blessing the people are proper responses
Leadership need not honor God publicly
questions.correctAnswer: Offerings and blessing the people are proper responses
questions.explanation: David’s burnt offerings, peace offerings, and blessing the people in the name of the LORD (vv. 17-18) demonstrate that worship includes sacrificial dedication and pastoral blessing, reflecting proper leadership before God (cf. Leviticus 22:29).

questions.question: What theological significance can be drawn from David’s statement in 2 Samuel 6:21 regarding his dancing before the LORD?
options: David’s worship is a response to God's sovereign choice and calling
David is indifferent to God's will
questions.correctAnswer: David’s worship is a response to God's sovereign choice and calling
questions.explanation: David explains that his worship is because the LORD chose him above Saul and his house to rule Israel (v21), showing that worship is a response to divine election and divine authority, a key theological principle.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s killing of Uzzah in 2 Samuel 6 shows divine cruelty. What does 2 Samuel 6:6-7 actually teach about God’s holiness and human sinfulness?
options: God’s holiness demands respect and shows consequences for disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands respect and shows consequences for disobedience
questions.explanation: The passage shows that God's holiness is inviolable and that disobedience, even if well-intended, has serious consequences, highlighting the seriousness of sin and the need for reverence (cf. Exodus 20:5; Hebrews 12:29).

questions.question: What does the movement of the ark from Gibeah to the city of David (2 Samuel 6:3-4, 12-15) reveal about the redemptive narrative in Israel’s history?
options: The ark’s relocation symbolizes God’s presence dwelling among His chosen people
The ark was moved for purely political reasons
The ark was ignored by Israel
The ark was a source of fear only
questions.correctAnswer: The ark’s relocation symbolizes God’s presence dwelling among His chosen people
questions.explanation: The ark's journey into David's city marks the centralization of worship and God's covenantal presence among Israel, foreshadowing Christ’s incarnation and God's dwelling with humanity (cf. John 1:14).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most emphasized by the naming of the place Perezuzzah in 2 Samuel 6:8?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wrath and justice
questions.explanation: David named the place Perezuzzah, meaning 'outburst against Uzzah,' emphasizing God's righteous anger and justice against irreverence toward His holiness (2 Samuel 6:8; cf. Nahum 1:2).

questions.question: What does the synthesis of David’s joyful worship (2 Samuel 6:14-15) and his blessing of the people (2 Samuel 6:18-19) indicate about sanctification and communal life?
options: Sanctification is individualistic and excludes community
Sanctified worship leads to blessing and care for the community
Worship is unrelated to social responsibility
Community life is unimportant in worship
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctified worship leads to blessing and care for the community
questions.explanation: David’s energetic worship and subsequent blessing and provision for the people demonstrate that true sanctification expresses itself both in personal devotion and communal generosity (cf. Acts 2:44-47).
